findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/Abelian.lean:29 `IsAbelianGalois.tower_bot [Algebra K L] [Algebra L M] [IsScalarTower K L M]`, of which line 56's `IntermediateField` instance is itself only the corollary; code/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/ArtinSymbol.lean:106 `artinSymbol_map_restrictNormalHom {M L : Type*} … [IsScalarTower K M L]`.
findings.fix: State `theorem commute_of_tower {M : Type*} [Field M] [Algebra K M] [Algebra M L] [IsScalarTower K M L] (hab : ∀ σ τ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, Commute σ τ) (σ τ : M ≃ₐ[K] M) : Commute σ τ`, proved by `have : IsAbelianGalois K L := {}; have : IsAbelianGalois K M := .tower_bot K M L; exact Commute.all σ τ`; the `IntermediateField` case is an instantiation.
findings.issue: `commute_of_intermediateField` is a strict specialization to `M : IntermediateField K L` of Mathlib's tower lemma it wraps, so it does not apply to a subextension presented as a field with `[Algebra K M] [Algebra M L] [IsScalarTower K M L]` — which is exactly how the repo's own `artinSymbol_map_restrictNormalHom` presents one.

findings.evidence: UnramifiedTower.lean:51-57 (`{M L : Type*} … [IsScalarTower K M L]`) versus :71-77 (`(M : IntermediateField K L)`), the latter's body being just `isUnramifiedAt_of_intermediateExtension (M := M) (L := L) v.asIdeal (hur v hv)`.
findings.fix: Generalize to `{M : Type*} [Field M] [NumberField M] [Algebra K M] [Algebra M L] [IsScalarTower K M L]`, matching line 51; the proof term is unchanged, and the roadmap's `isUnramifiedAway_of_intermediateField M S hur` still elaborates through the `CoeSort`. Then state `artinHomAway_restrict` at the same tower level as `artinSymbol_map_restrictNormalHom`.
findings.issue: Same defect: `isUnramifiedAway_of_intermediateField` takes `M : IntermediateField K L` although its own base lemma twenty lines above, `isUnramifiedAt_of_intermediateExtension`, is stated for an abstract tower and is applied unchanged. `artinHomAway_restrict` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Ideal/ArtinMap.lean:228) inherits both restrictions and so cannot be used for a subextension given as a field.

findings.evidence: ArtinMap.lean:88-90 uses only `hur v hv`, i.e. unramifiedness at `v`; `artinSymbol` itself is already stated per prime with exactly that hypothesis (ArtinSymbol.lean:50-53).
findings.fix: Define the prime-local `artinElement hab (𝔭 : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [𝔭.IsMaximal] (hur : ∀ (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭], Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q) : L ≃ₐ[K] L` with `artinSymbol_eq_mk_artinElement`, `isArithFrobAt_artinElement` and `artinElement_eq_of_isArithFrobAt` at that level, and set `artinElementAway hab S hur v = if v ∈ S then 1 else artinElement hab v.asIdeal (hur v hv)`, deriving the current lemmas from them.
findings.issue: The abelian collapse `ConjClasses.mkEquiv.symm (artinSymbol 𝔭 hur)` is a statement about one unramified prime, but it is only exposed through `artinElementAway`, which carries `S` and unramifiedness at every prime outside `S`. Consequently `isArithFrobAt_artinElementAway` (line 110) and `artinElementAway_eq_of_isArithFrobAt` (line 125) — both facts about a single `v` — require the global hypothesis, and a caller holding one unramified prime cannot name its Frobenius element without inventing an `S`.

summary: The Artin map itself sits at the right level, but the two new subextension helpers are specialized to `IntermediateField K L` although the Mathlib lemma and the repo lemmas they wrap are stated for an abstract tower, and the abelian collapse of the Artin symbol to a single automorphism — a prime-local fact — is only available bundled with `S` and the global unramifiedness hypothesis.
